s1.syndrome_frame: chronic swelling and discomfort in the oral cavity with fluctuating pain intensity and sensation of heaviness
salient_findings: slowly growing swelling in the right upper vestibule
firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa
mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices
key_facts: 45-year-old woman
2-month history of symptoms
swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule
fluctuations in pain intensity
sensation of heaviness in the area
teeth #15 and #16 are grossly carious
no tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth
mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices
preoperative blood tests are within normal limits
gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue obtained during curettage

shortlist.label: Periapical granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: histopathological examination of curettage tissue and clinical presentation of chronic swelling and discomfort

shortlist.label: Periapical cyst
shortlist.why_kept: mild periapical radiolucency and chronic nature of symptoms

shortlist.label: Periapical abscess
shortlist.why_kept: initial provisional diagnosis and presence of swelling and discomfort

shortlist.label: Radicular cyst
shortlist.why_kept: similar clinical presentation and possible progression from periapical granuloma

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of swelling and discomfort in the oral cavity, although less likely given the presence of carious teeth

raw.rationale: The presence of a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue obtained during curettage and the clinical presentation of a slowly growing swelling with fluctuations in pain intensity are more consistent with a periapical granuloma, which is a collection of granulation tissue in response to pulp necrosis, rather than an abscess or cyst.

rejected.label: Periapical abscess
rejected.why: The lack of tenderness on percussion and the absence of a clear fluctuant mass suggest it is not an abscess.

rejected.label: Periapical cyst
rejected.why: The clinical and radiographic findings do not strongly support a cyst, which typically presents with a well-defined radiolucency and may not have the same type of tissue obtained during curettage.

rejected.label: Radicular cyst
rejected.why: Similar to the periapical cyst, the findings do not strongly support a radicular cyst, which is essentially the same entity as a periapical cyst but with a specific origin from the root.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: The location and the involvement of teeth #15 and #16, which are not associated with an unerupted tooth, make this diagnosis less likely.
